pattern: Specify-written requirements retain STEP-only authorship (issue #22)
evidence: Issue #22 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/22) explicitly requires a stable STEP-only marker on Specify-authored PMI and recognition by existing.rs. Rust adds provenance=specify-core:written:v1 only for marked requirements; Python has no such field. The pinned haecceity alpha.8 reader exposes tolerance descriptions and per-item consumed IDs; the other markers require raw Document slots or inverse DESCRIPTION_ATTRIBUTE references to those IDs. tests/pmi_provenance.rs checks default PMI on GRM-02 (using the committed shaft fixture when absent from the corpus, without explicit thread answers), and explicit M2/M3 threads and straight knurl on corpus GRM-03 when available. An exported corpus missing GRM-03 fails. The tests also cover emitted requirement kinds, repeated writes, reserved UDA metadata, two sizes on one aspect without identifier tags, EXPRESS validity and byte preservation of imported NIST AP242 PMI on a shared face. docs/pmi-provenance.md specifies exact fields and matching rules. Frozen Python oracle captures are retained.

pattern: no Rust-written file: Python's intents name parts the Rust engine does not have
evidence: NIST CTC-02 and CTC-04: OpenCascade's XCAF makes a part of each shape representation of one product (the solid and its surface models: 3 and 2 parts), haecceity one part per product with all its faces (question Q7; existing.json and the part stream's entries). Python's accept-defaults intents are bound to parts 1 and 2 of its numbering, which the Rust engine's reading of the file does not have, so examples/write_fixtures.rs refuses the case before calling the writer (its part-index check; the message is rust.refused.txt) rather than write an intent onto the wrong part; Python itself refuses the write of these files ('this assembly already has PMI not written by specify-core', write.json). Nothing to cross until Q7 is settled; an intent made by the Rust engine's own analysis of these files is the CLI stream's to write.

pattern: the part's default finish, written as a surface texture, is not read by specify-core (Python)
evidence: The Rust writer writes the part's default finish (Ra 3.2 on every accept-defaults intent) as ISO 10303-1110's surface texture on the part's product_definition_shape (property_definition 'surface texture', material removal 'any process allowed', its parameter a surface_texture_representation of 'measuring method' 'Ra' and 'characteristic value' 3.2 µm; question Q3, decided 2026-10-09; haecceity checks surface_texture_representation WR1-WR5 and general_property_association WR1-WR2 on its writes, quiddity-rust c228f95), and reads it back as the part's surface_finish (src/existing.rs). specify-core's part_settings finds the default finish only in its own text route, a DESCRIPTIVE_REPRESENTATION_ITEM('surface texture','Ra 3.2 µm unless otherwise specified') (existing.py), and OpenCascade's XCAF has no surface texture model, so Python reads none, on every Rust-written part of a single-part file (assemblies report no settings in either engine). The form is AP242's standard one, the text route is not (haecceity decision 5); the gap is Python's reader.

pattern: a thread written as AP242's thread feature is not read by specify-core (Python)
evidence: The Rust writer writes each thread as AP242's `thread` (side, major diameter, form, class, hand, partial area; haecceity checks thread WR1-WR16 on every write) with its pitch and depths as a user defined attribute set (UDA practice §5-7; upstream need U8), and reads it back as the intent's thread. specify-core's existing.notes reads threads only from its own 'manufacturing requirement' text route (existing.py, notes), and OpenCascade's XCAF has no thread model, so Python reads none of them (6 threads in the probes of plate, pin, stack, assembly and a_hole_along_x). The AP242 schema form is standard, the text route is not (haecceity decision 5), but no CAx-IF practice for thread features was found to cite, and the pitch has no semantic home in haecceity yet (U8). A thread therefore does not cross from the Rust engine to the Python one.

pattern: a fit written as its ISO 286 class reads with no limits in specify-core (Python)
evidence: Every fit the Rust writer writes reads back in Python with its nominal value and no upper or lower deviation: the stack's Ø8 H7 bores ([9] of parts 0 and 1, +0.015/0) and Ø8 h6 pin ([3] of part 2, 0/-0.009), and the H11 clearance hole sets on several faces (the plate's and the assembly's Ø6.6, +0.09/0; NIST CTC-03's Ø4.7625 on the 8 faces of hole_patterns.rectangle, the four corner holes, the identical holes and the stack's part 1, +0.075/0), which OpenCascade now reads on all their faces (haecceity writes one geometric_item_specific_usage per face since quiddity-rust c228f95, question Q20 (2)). The Rust writer writes a fit as plus_minus_tolerance -> limits_and_fits('H','hole','7','') (PMI practice §5.2.5), after checking the intent's limits are the class's (src/writer.rs); haecceity's reader reads the class. specify-core's read_existing takes limits only from IsDimWithPlusMinusTolerance (existing.py) and never asks XCAF for the class of tolerance, so the fit's meaning is lost on the Python side. Python's own files carry the fit as bare limits, which is what OCCT's writer forced (docs/design.md, 'What is written').

path: python_written.resume[rust did not resume: fingerprint differs only in signs of zero]
pattern: the Rust engine finds Python-written schema 1 answers but refuses them on the schema 1 fingerprint: zeros' signs differ
evidence: On every part of the 11 Python-written synthetic files (tests/fixtures/oracle/parts/**/written.step.gz) resume::stored reads Python's payload (schema 1), equal to what Python's own resume.saved finds (python_written_evidence.json.gz), with the same face count; the stored fingerprint is specify-core's own schema 1 hash of the faces it lists (fingerprint_v1 in the evidence), and those faces equal the Rust engine's by value, differing only in signs of zero (faces_gap), which schema 1's text keeps. Q14 (decided 2026-10-09) keeps schema 1 read exactly as before: resumed only when its own fingerprint matches, so the Rust engine is right not to resume these. The fix is schema 2, which both engines write: specify-core's own schema 2 fingerprint (branch fingerprint-v2, captured 2026-10-10) of its faces in these files equals the Rust engine's on all 15 parts (tests/cross_engine.rs schema_two_fingerprints_are_the_same_in_both_engines), so files specify-core writes with schema 2 resume here. These files were written by the oracle's specify-core (cc341dd, schema 1) and are not rewritten by the recapture. Everything else these files hold (existing PMI, part settings) reads in Rust exactly as Python reads it.

path: fingerprint_v2[fingerprint differs: faces differ in kind or rounded centroid]
pattern: the faces' rounded centroids differ where haecceity's face integrals are off (U11), so the schema 2 fingerprints differ
evidence: Python's faces (python_meta.json.gz, resume_evidence) and the Rust engine's faces of the Rust-written file agree in kind and count (156) and in every centroid rounded to 3 decimals but those of faces 93, 97, 109 and 112 (B-spline surfaces: Python [-145.171, 51.241, 52.431], Rust -145.170814, 51.239719, 52.431061) and 98, 103, 104 and 108 (spheres: Python 72.111, Rust 72.111586 rounds to 72.112). OpenCascade's adaptive integral (eps 1e-9) of the same faces gives 51.24061051 and 72.11149644, Python's values: features.json judges each of these eight centroids rust-wrong (faces[93].centroid[*] etc., upstream need U11, Part::face_moments to 1e-6). The fingerprint itself is not at fault: on the other 34 parts of the check, where the rounded faces are the same, specify-core's own schema 2 fingerprint (branch fingerprint-v2) equals the Rust engine's byte for byte (schema_two_fingerprints_are_the_same_in_both_engines). No answers are stored in a NIST file the Rust writer writes, so nothing fails to resume here; answers stored on this part would not cross engines until U11 is met.

pattern: Specify's own dimensions under the general tolerance (nominal only, #63) are not read back as existing PMI
evidence: Issue #63 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/63): the writer writes the dimensions the general tolerance covers (general.rs: plain sizes, plane levels and hole locations) with their nominal alone, so the STEP states every dimension a drawing would. existing.rs skips a dimension that is both Specify-marked (specify-core:written:v1) and nominal only: it states nothing the geometry does not, and read back without its answers it must not settle a question (tests/writer.rs pmi_is_added_to_a_part_that_has_some). Python reads every dimension, so each such dimension is in Python's existing list and not in Rust's. Every difference here is a Size_Diameter or Location_LinearDistance with no upper or lower; the toleranced and basic dimensions agree.

pattern: The independent Python reader does not expose characteristic ID_ATTRIBUTE values
evidence: quiddity-rust#137 (v0.2.6) requires recapturing the writer fixtures for presentation and the new aspect shapes; the current writer also includes #65's numeric ID_ATTRIBUTE records and number history. The documented cc341dd + ISO/fingerprint Python reference does not read requirement identifiers. Its recaptured readback is unchanged, while Rust reads the numbers on the actual semantic roots (#135 exposes the same ids). Measured: 97 newly visible number-field differences on 10 parts after the existing semantic difference entries are applied: NIST CTC-03 (1), a_hole_along_x (2), assembly parts 0/1 (19/3), four_corner_holes (12), identical_holes (8), pin (3), plate (19), stack parts 0/1 (15/15). tests/characteristic_numbers.rs verifies the standard slots, uniqueness, history, face supports and rewrite stability, including separate datum/size and composite/location aspects, and the frozen category-order input. This entry covers only the Python API's absent number field; no semantic values or face targets are projected out. Analysis/read hashes of unchanged inputs remain unchanged.

pattern: The independent Python reader predates Specify's dimension origin/source UDAs
evidence: Specify #77 (PR #78) adds a specify pmi origin UDA to each newly written size/location. Recapturing the quiddity-rust#137 v0.2.6 writer fixtures changes 12 STEP outputs and their SHA metadata, while the documented cc341dd + ISO/fingerprint Python reader returns exactly the same readbacks: it does not expose this UDA. Measured after existing semantic entries: 69 absent origin fields on eight parts: NIST CTC-03 (1), assembly part 0 (15), four_corner_holes (9), identical_holes (5), plate (15), stack parts 0/1/2 (11/12/1). Rust reads requirement origin on these dimensions. tests/pmi_origin.rs additionally checks every newly written dimension including general-tolerance dimensions, the actual DIMENSIONAL_SIZE/DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION UDA owner under split datum/size and composite/location aspects, exact readback, no-op bytes and changed-value rewrites. Frozen v0.2.4 inputs and legacy analysis/read hashes remain unchanged. Only this absent API field is covered; no dimensional value or support is projected out.

pattern: The independent Python reader predates Specify's dimension origin/source UDAs
evidence: Specify #77 (PR #78) stores the measurement source alongside dimension origin in a UDA on the characteristic root. The independent Python reference predates that UDA; recaptured Python readbacks are byte-identical despite the 12 changed quiddity-rust#137 v0.2.6 STEP outputs. Measured after existing semantic entries: 69 absent source fields, paired with the 69 absent origin fields on NIST CTC-03 (1), assembly part 0 (15), four_corner_holes (9), identical_holes (5), plate (15), stack parts 0/1/2 (11/12/1). Rust's sources retain schema 2, the resume face fingerprint, measured face supports and measurement parameter. tests/pmi_origin.rs verifies source stability on re-run, changed-value rewrites, frozen v0.2.4 specimens and split sized datums/composite sizes/location aspects. Only the missing source field is covered; dimensional semantics and face matching remain compared.
